summary.summary: Don Etherton called Arizona Roofers asking if they could replace some “piled roof pieces” on his roof in Wickhamberg. The representative explained that if it is just placing/replacing tiles, the scope is smaller than what their company typically takes on and suggested using a roofing repair specialist/handyman instead. The rep could not recommend a specific provider but advised Don to search Google using his city plus “roofing handyman specialist” to find direct contacts, noting Arizona Roofers is currently booking 4–8 weeks out and a repair specialist would likely be faster and more cost-effective for a minor repair. Don thanked the rep and ended the call without scheduling service.
key_points: Customer (Don Etherton) requested replacement of some roof pieces/tiles on his roof in Wickhamberg.
Rep stated small tile-placement/minor repair work is generally smaller than Arizona Roofers’ typical job scope and suggested using a roofing repair specialist/handyman.
Rep noted their current lead time is about 4–8 weeks and advised the customer to Google his city plus “roofing handyman specialist”; no appointment was booked.
action_items: Customer to search for and contact a local roofing repair specialist/handyman via Google using the suggested search terms.
next_steps: Customer to reach out to a repair specialist for the minor tile/piece replacement.
If the issue is larger than expected, customer can call Arizona Roofers back to discuss a broader scope project.

pending_actions.raw_text: I recommend going on Google specifically and typing in your city and then roofing handyman specialist, all three words

issues: Did not capture or verify contact information (phone/email) or service address.
Did not ask clarifying needs-discovery questions (extent of damage, how long issue has existed, roof type/height, safety/access constraints) before determining it was out of scope.
Did not offer an inspection/estimate option or explain any minimum job size policy; the customer was effectively turned away without a clear internal process for small repairs.
Could not provide a specific referral despite being asked; only suggested a generic Google search (missed opportunity to follow a referral/partner SOP if one exists).
No explicit objection-handling occurred; however, the rep did not probe to confirm whether the customer would still want to proceed given the 4–8 week timeline.
positive_behaviors: Professional greeting with company name and representative name.
Identified potential fit issue and set expectations about current scheduling timeline (4–8 weeks).
Provided an alternative path for the customer (suggested searching for a repair specialist/handyman) to help resolve the issue faster and more cost-effectively.
Maintained a courteous, respectful tone and closed the call politely.
